claim: Blending theory is described as four spaces (two inputs, generic, blend) with emergent structure in the blend; the theory has no single measurable criterion for a good blend, and its author defends it with argument and in-sample generalisation, not decisive experiments.
agent_test: Run the same task with and without an explicit written generic-space step (name the shared abstraction before merging); score blend validity by blind judges at equal tokens.
audit_note: Absence of a single criterion is an inference: Veale et al. say Fauconnier and Turner give five non-orthogonal optimality constraints, and Turner's page says evidence is mostly in-sample generalisation tested out of sample while experiments (McCubbins and Turner 2013) exist but are hard.

claim: Human emergent attributes in combined concepts are rare under strict scoring (Hampton 1987: 3 of 174; lenient 11) and most apparent emergents come from retrieving familiar instances or category stretching (Hampton 1989: only 6 of 51 attributes reached 10% or more).
agent_test: Check whether our agent's claimed emergent features survive a test of being retrievable from one input alone; count false emergents.

claim: Among attributes false of both constituents, 35% (22 of 63) were judged true of the conjunction (Hampton, Dillon et al.), so emergence is real but modest.
agent_test: Measure the fraction of blend properties true of neither input that independent judges accept as true of the blend.

claim: LLMs are weaker at blending than at association or analogy: valid rates 43.4% (blend) vs 53.4% (analogy) vs 59.0% (association) across 35 LLMs. Re-checked against the paper text.
agent_test: Give our agent blend, analogy and association items at equal tokens and compare valid rates; expect blends lowest.

claim: Frontier LLMs beat lay humans on valid blends (43.4% vs 12.8%; N=75 Prolific adults), but humans' skipped items were scored zero, so the gap is inflated and says nothing about experts.
agent_test: Do not claim superhuman creativity from this; compare against our own plain-model arm.

claim: The bottleneck in LLM blending is finding a valid generic space (43.4%); once found, a coherent blend follows 97.1% of the time (abstraction gap).
agent_test: Add an explicit generic-space proposal and validity check before blending; compare valid-blend rate with a plain prompt at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs show inventive homogeneity: 19.9% (412/2,070) of invented concepts reuse 2 or more properties from other models; blends are about 14 times more likely to be reused than analogies at level 2; same-provider models reuse 2.3 times more. Reuse and homogeneity are also found in other tasks: LLM variability 0.459 vs human 0.738 (AUT), and GPT-4o recipe merges repeat ingredients (56% smoked paprika).
agent_test: Sample several blends per item; measure property overlap across runs; add an exclusion list of already-used properties and check gain at equal tokens.
audit_note: The 56% smoked paprika figure is for GPT-4o asked for a general creative recipe, not a recipe merge (merges show fixation separately); 0.459 vs 0.738 is the v3 value.

claim: Performance on association, analogy and blending correlates across 35 models (mean cross-task r 0.47; association vs analogy originality r 0.73), but the unit is the model, not the item.
agent_test: Evaluate blending separately; do not assume one combinatorial skill.

claim: LLM judge panels are only moderately reliable for blend quality: ICC 0.67 for integration quality, 0.48 for one utility measure; panel agrees with humans 75% on unanimous items; in research ideation LLM vs human Pearson was 0.159.
agent_test: Use human spot checks of blend judgments; never rely on one LLM judge.
audit_note: The 75% agreement is on unanimous items only (panel majority agrees with humans 66% overall, n=96 on unanimous); ICC bands are 'fair to good' by Cicchetti.

claim: LLMs poorly recognise emergent property types in noun-phrase combinations: GPT-4o type accuracy 56.4% vs human 81%; noun-phrase completion emergence scores for baseline LLMs stay far below human 38.0 and gold 59.9 (CCPT, 12,315 instances).
agent_test: Test our agent on emergent vs canceled property induction; check whether a verifier step lifts type accuracy.

claim: Iterated self-refinement adds little for emergent properties: emergent E 45.1 to 45.8 over 5 iterations, canceled 60.5 to 63.3; the gap to gold stays large.
agent_test: Compare 1 vs 5 refinement rounds against 5 independent samples at equal total tokens.

claim: A theory-informed generator plus filter helped human creators in a narrow task: PopBlends gave 2.03 vs 0.87 ideas per pair (N=10, Wilcoxon p<0.001) and lower mental demand, yet GPT-3 attribute accuracy was only 57%, so filtering was needed.
agent_test: Pair a generator with a cheap filter (connector relates to both inputs) and measure valid blends per token.

claim: Theory-guided prompting (blending-theory text, diagnosis and transfer agents) raised judged ingenuity in image metaphors (2.75 direct, 3.69 strong prompt, 4.56 full; N=100), but table and text disagree slightly (4.56 vs 4.61) and judges are partly LLMs.
agent_test: Ablate the blending-theory text in our prompt against a strong generic prompt at equal tokens.

claim: In vision-language models, concept-level combination is strong but rendering often fails: GPT-4o combined concepts in 90% of 40 DALLE-3 examples, then 27.8% (10/36) failed to render; implication win rate GPT-4o 73.5 vs experts 78.3 and average people 51.0.
agent_test: Report concept step and execution step separately.

claim: Diffusion-model interpolation is not reliable blending: at ratio 0.5 blended-concept depiction is 0.621 (mixed 0.862), but over all ratios 0.389 (0.471); one concept often dominates. Verified.
agent_test: Warning only; mixing ratio is not selective blending.

claim: No image-blending method is uniformly best in a user study (100 participants, 22 pairs): ALTERNATE over SWITCH 51% (p=0.31); results depend on category.
agent_test: Report results per category when testing blend variants.

claim: Neural (N400) evidence for blending-like processing of novel metaphors rests on small samples (N=18, N=13) and the originals were not opened; unsettled. A later ERP study (N=35) found the metaphor N400 effect only for low-concreteness metaphors; no direct replication of the 2002 study was found.
agent_test: None; background only.

claim: Claims that blending prompts induce awakening or hallucination transitions in LLMs are unsupported: no controlled data, and fused vs non-fused prompts did not differ significantly.
agent_test: If tested, require a non-fused control and blind scoring at equal tokens.

claim: Computational blending architectures (Divago, Goguen, Eppe, Besold, Diaconescu) were evaluated on hand-built examples without benchmarks or human data; whether formal blending beats plain LLM generation is untested.
agent_test: Compare a generic-space-first procedure against a plain prompt on Schapiro-style items.

claim: Evaluation of LLM blending is mostly LLM-judged and domain-shifted (images, lay humans), so effect sizes for text blending in reasoning tasks are unknown.
agent_test: Build a small human-judged blend set in our own task domain before trusting blend scores.
audit_note: Absence claim ('effect sizes unknown') cannot be proven by these sources; they do show LLM-panel judging (Schapiro, Lu), image tasks (Peng) and lay Prolific humans (Schapiro, N=75).

claim: Temperature is a weak lever for diversity or novelty of LLM creative output: novelty slope 0.308 with coherence loss 0.240 (Llama 2-Chat 70B stories); GPT-4o idea diversity 0.618 at T=0 to 0.679 at T=1; above T=1 GPT-4o gives gibberish.
agent_test: Do not spend tokens on temperature to reduce blend reuse; measure it against a persona or constraint arm at equal tokens.
audit_note: Peeperkorn calls the coherence relation with temperature 'moderate' (.240) and the novelty one 'weak' (.308); Terwiesch: GPT-4o diversity 0.618 (T=0) to 0.679 (T=1), nonsensical above 1.0, matching.

claim: Injecting random personas or random constraints raises GPT-4o idea diversity close to human level (0.757 and 0.735 vs human 0.773, zero-shot 0.679). A 'be creative' system prompt does not (LLM variability 0.576 vs human 0.738 at the strongest setting). Iterative 'bolder' refinement lowers diversity (0.575).
agent_test: Give each blend attempt a different random persona or constraint; compare reuse rate with and without.

claim: Explicit structured recombination beats plain GPT-4o for novelty and diversity in recipe hybrids (novelty 3.53 vs 3.146, p=0.0009; 3.612 vs 3.141, p=9.2e-8), with slightly lower value (85% vs 98% valuable in the open task). Plain GPT-4o produces shallow merges.
agent_test: Test a blend step that maps both inputs to a structured form and merges roles, versus a plain 'combine these' prompt, with blind judges.

claim: Abstraction-first prompting helps reasoning but the abstraction is itself a failure point: Step-Back lifts PaLM-2L MMLU Physics 66.4% to 73.2% and Chemistry 70.9% to 81.8%, yet corrects 20.5% of baseline errors while adding 11.9% new ones. No study tests an explicit generic-space step inside a blend.
agent_test: Add a verification of the stated shared abstraction before merging; measure how often it rejects.

claim: No measured result exists for blending as a stuck-state operator in problem solving. Nearest results are candidate aggregation (Mixture-of-Agents 65.1% vs 57.5% AlpacaEval 2.0) and abstraction or analogy prompting.
agent_test: Run a stuck-state operator that merges two failed approaches against a restart and a best-of-N arm on a reasoning benchmark.

claim: GPT-2 predicts the human emergent property for only 7 of 15 Murphy (1988) items; no study compares modern LLM and human emergent-feature rates on shared pairs. No expert baseline for textual blends and no judge setup with ICC above 0.8 was found.
agent_test: Run our own comparison: LLM conjunction attributes versus Hampton-style human lists on shared pairs; report agreement of judges.
